titre: The summit farthest from the center of the Earth
accroche: Everest is the highest summit in the world above sea level. An Ecuadorian volcano is the one farthest from the Earth's center.
contenu_vulgarise:
On June 23, 1802, Alexander von Humboldt, the French botanist Aimé Bonpland, and the Ecuadorian nobleman Carlos Montúfar begin the ascent of Chimborazo, a volcano that learned Europe then holds to be the highest summit in the world. A crevasse stops them about three hundred meters from the top, but they have already passed 5,800 meters, without modern equipment: an altitude record that will stand for about thirty years, until the first precise surveys of the Himalayas shift the title of highest summit in the world elsewhere.

## An Earth wider than it is tall

Humboldt climbs, without knowing it, on ground already contested. Half a century earlier, between 1735 and 1744, a French geodetic mission led by Charles-Marie de La Condamine, Pierre Bouguer, and Louis Godin had chosen this same region, then the province of Quito, to settle a scientific debate: is the Earth elongated at the poles, as Descartes thought, or flattened, as Newton predicted? By measuring an arc of meridian at the equator and comparing the result with a measurement taken in Lapland, the mission proves Newton right: the planet is not a perfect sphere. It is a spheroid slightly flattened at the poles and bulging at the equator. The distance between the Earth's center and its surface is therefore not constant; it varies with latitude, not only with elevation.

## Another record, invisible to the naked eye

It is this difference that reshuffles the cards for the “highest” summit. Everest towers over everything from sea level, at 8,848 meters. But it lies at a high northern latitude, far from the equatorial bulge. Chimborazo, for its part, tops out at 6,268 meters, 2,580 meters less, at a little more than one degree south of the equator, almost at the crest of the bulge that Newton had divined by calculation. A GNSS measurement campaign carried out in 2016 by the Institut de recherche pour le développement (Research Institute for Development), Ecuador's Military Geographic Institute, and the National Polytechnic School measures the summit's elevation at 6,268 meters. The American agency NOAA adopts the same value, and places the summit of Chimborazo more than 2,072 meters farther from the Earth's center than that of Everest. It is, over the entire surface of the Earth, the point farthest from the planet's center.

## What “high” means

Chimborazo does not dethrone Everest: elevation is measured from sea level, a convention that remains the right one for comparing mountains with one another. But it is a reminder that a convention is not a brute fact. “High” and “far from the center of the Earth” coincide almost everywhere on the globe, except near the equator, where the very shape of the planet shifts the answer. Humboldt, in 1802, was looking for the summit of the world without the instruments to measure that gap; it took two centuries and satellites in orbit to put a number on it.

carte.punch: 2,580 m lower than Everest, Chimborazo is nonetheless farther from the Earth's center.
carte.idee: Chimborazo, in Ecuador, tops out at 6,268 meters, 2,580 meters lower than Everest. But set a little more than one degree from the equator, on the Earth's bulge, its summit is farther from the planet's center than Everest's, by more than 2,072 meters.

quiz.question: Why is the summit of Chimborazo farther from the Earth's center than that of Everest, even though it stands 2,580 meters lower?
choix: Because the Earth is not a perfect sphere: it bulges at the equator, where Chimborazo is, and is flattened at the poles
Because satellites measure Chimborazo more precisely than Everest, which has not been remeasured since 1852
Because Chimborazo is a volcano and is measured from its base, whereas Everest is measured from sea level
Because Everest erodes every year while Chimborazo keeps growing
quiz.explication: The Earth's rotation makes it bulge at the equator: the Earth's radius is larger there than at the poles. Located one degree from the equator, Chimborazo benefits from this bulge, whereas Everest is far from it. Both summits are measured the same way, from sea level. What differs is the shape of the Earth beneath their feet.

The botanist Aimé Bonpland and the Ecuadorian nobleman Carlos Montúfar

quiz_supplementaire.question: What stopped Humboldt, Bonpland, and Montúfar before they reached the summit of Chimborazo?
choix: A crevasse, about three hundred meters from the summit
A snowstorm that lasted several days
Lack of oxygen, which made Bonpland lose consciousness
A disagreement with local authorities over the ascent
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text specifies that a crevasse stops them about three hundred meters from the summit, after they had already passed 5,800 meters without modern equipment.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What did the French geodetic mission led between 1735 and 1744 in the Chimborazo region establish?
choix: That Chimborazo is the highest point in the world above sea level
That the Earth's radius is identical at every point on the globe
That Chimborazo is a still-active volcano, unlike Everest
That the Earth is flattened at the poles and bulging at the equator, confirming Newton against Descartes
quiz_supplementaire.explication: By comparing an arc of meridian measured at the equator with a measurement taken in Lapland, the mission proves Newton right against Descartes: the Earth is a spheroid flattened at the poles.
